toc.title: The exam, its scope and how this course works

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Describe the exam: its length, question types and how it is scored
  • Say what the exam guide covers and why you should read the current version
  • Name the four domains and their weights
  • Know who the exam is for and what it leaves out
  • Use the tags, case, Design Checks and questions of this course

2The exam, its scope and how this course works

Running case

Meet Tidewater Outfitters

  • Tidewater Outfitters is a fictional online shop for outdoor gear, run by a small team
  • Its founder wants everyone to understand the cloud well enough to make sound choices
  • The shop is moving from a rented server room to AWS, one decision at a time
  • You will follow each decision: access, security, storage, databases, networks and costs
  • Your job: learn what each AWS service is for, and when to choose it

The Exam at a Glance

  • 65 questions: 50 are scored and 15 are unscored trial questions
  • You cannot tell which are unscored, so treat every question as real
  • 90 minutes in all: about 83 seconds a question
  • Your result is a scaled score from 100 to 1,000, and 700 passes

Exam tip

The 15 unscored questions are not marked on screen, so give every question your full attention.

Question Types and Scoring

  • Multiple choice: one correct answer and three distractors
  • Multiple response: two or more correct answers out of five or more options; the question tells you how many to pick
  • An unanswered question counts as wrong, and there is no penalty for guessing, so answer every one
  • Compensatory scoring: you must pass the exam as a whole, not each section
  • Section feedback on the score report is general, and AWS says to read it with care
  • The guide does not say how multiple-response questions are marked
Exam tip

Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank always scores zero.

Booking, Taking and Keeping the Credential [Verify live]

  • Fee: USD 100, with possible extra costs such as exchange rates
  • Delivery: at a Pearson VUE test center or online with a proctor
  • Languages: several, including English; the Italian and German versions retire after 31 December 2026
  • Valid for 3 years; renew by passing the latest version of the exam or an Associate or Professional exam
  • No prerequisites
  • As of 4 November 2026: check AWS's certification page for price, languages and delivery
Exam tip

Fees, languages and renewal rules change; read AWS's page before you book.

The Exam Guide Is Your Scope [Dates]

  • The exam guide lists the domains, weights, task statements and in-scope services
  • This course follows version 1.3, published on 29 October 2026
  • The guide had four versions in 2026: 24 June, 28 August, 24 September and 29 October
  • AWS publishes changes about a month before they reach the exam
  • The service list is non-exhaustive and subject to change
  • The guide outranks this course on scope
Exam tip

Read the current exam guide before you book and again in the last week.

Four Domains, Nineteen Task Statements

  • Domain 1, Cloud Concepts: 24%, four task statements
  • Domain 2, Security and Compliance: 30%, four
  • Domain 3, Cloud Technology and Services: 34%, eight
  • Domain 4, Billing, Pricing, and Support: 12%, three
  • Weights are shares of scored content; the guide gives no weights below the domain

Exam tip

Domains 1 and 2 together are more than half of the exam.

Who the Exam Is For

  • The target candidate has up to six months of exposure to AWS Cloud design, implementation or operations
  • It may be someone early in a cloud career, or someone who works with people in cloud roles
  • It is foundational and not tied to a job role
  • Out of scope for the candidate: coding, designing cloud architecture, troubleshooting, implementation, and load and performance testing
  • Task statements use verbs such as define, identify and understand
Exam tip

Learn what each service is for and when to choose it; setting it up step by step is not what is tested.

How This Course Works

  • 17 modules: this introduction, 14 content modules in the guide's order, a recap and an exam-technique module
  • Each content module has what you will learn, a Tidewater case, Exam Tips, a recap and practice questions
  • A Design Check in each module, and a few optional Try it labs
  • Slide tags: Beyond the guide, Old name, Verify live, Dates
  • About one question in five is multiple response here: that share is this course's choice, not AWS's

Independent Course, Official Sources

  • This course is independent: not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon Web Services
  • It shows no AWS logos or service icons; service names appear as text
  • The notes and questions are in our own wording; it uses no AWS exam questions or dumps
  • AWS documentation and the exam guide outrank this course on every fact and rule
  • Names, prices and limits change: check the source on every Verify-live slide
Exam tip

When this course and the current AWS documentation disagree, the documentation wins.

3Quick Reference Card

  • Study one module, then do its questions; the modules follow the exam guide's order
  • Cover every task statement: the guide does not weight them separately
  • Read the exam guide before you book and again in the last week
  • Answer all 65 questions on the day; never leave one blank
  • This course is independent and educational: the official sources outrank it
Exam tip

Before you book, read AWS's current exam guide and certification page.
